baselineBeforeThisWave.note: These 19 are the 'known Windows failures'. (An earlier reading of '33 fail' came from a polluted run and is superseded by this deduped measurement.)

skips: pre-existing: '§9.4 — the ONE render boundary strips control characters' (a C0 filename cannot exist on win32)
pre-existing: 'clean file passes (exit 0)' and 'comment file triggers detection (exit 2)' (the comment-checker dependency is not installed)
ADDED BY THIS WAVE, with its reason: 'autoCheck: the hook resolves a relative file_path against the session workspace'

groups.productionDefect: packages/mpd-mcp-shared/log-sink.ts `owningRoot` built its containment prefix as `${root}/` with a HARD-CODED forward slash while `file` comes from `join`, so on win32 (`C:\…`) the comparison NEVER matched and every root was reported as `null` even though the sink had opened and was writing the file. Fixed with the platform's own containment test: `relative(root, file)` plus `isAbsolute`.
testFixes: the two env-chain arms now build their expectations with `resolve(...)`, stating the contract (absolute, in precedence order) instead of a POSIX spelling

the '(POSIX)' descriptor-rebind arm is platform-aware: POSIX keeps `rebind=rebound` + an untouched capture file; win32 asserts the DOCUMENTED `rebind=unsupported`, that the writer-based capture still logs the child's own stderr, and that the grandchild's raw fd write lands in the inherited capture file and NOT the log

rootCauses: four expectations spelled POSIX paths (`/elsewhere/.mpd/boulder.json`, `/ws/.mpd/boulder.json`, `WORKSPACE + "/.mpd/boulder.json"`, `/ws/.mpd/team/teams`) while production builds them with `join`

the C7 fixtures derived a file name with `path.slice(path.lastIndexOf("/") + 1)` — on win32 the path carries `\`, the search missed (-1), the 'name' became the WHOLE path, every lookup threw ENOENT and a present record read as `{leading:false, members:0}`; now `basename(path)`

the 'real ledger' arm read the GITIGNORED `.mpd/boulder.json` with an unguarded `readFileSync` and threw ENOENT on a tree without it; the contract is now asserted from a FIXTURE (a COMPLETED work reads inactive) and the real ledger is an extra reading only when it exists

groups.rootCause: the arms built a REAL `ChangeFeed({debounceMs:20})`, so ONE store write produced TWO observations — the in-process hook and the directory event — and an arm passed only while both landed inside the same fixed window. On POSIX that holds; on win32 the directory event arrives after the window and opens a SECOND one, so 'a store write reaches a subscriber' saw 2 calls instead of 1.
groups.fix: the six S-b feeds take an INERT watch door (`watch: inertWatch`), making the observation source deterministic; the watcher's real behaviour stays pinned by the S-c/S-d arms and by every arm that writes raw bytes with no store call.

groups.rootCause: the arm asserted the POSIX mode-bit rule (`chmod 0o644` ⇒ rejected) while `isExecutableFile` DOCUMENTS the win32 bound: 'the win32 arm accepts any regular file… the probe is name-based'. The sibling arm — an extensionless `chmod 0o755` file that must RESOLVE — passes on win32, i.e. the two were unsatisfiable together.
groups.fix: the arm now asserts the documented bound on win32 (the inert file IS accepted) and keeps the platform-independent 'absent ⇒ null' clause exact; a probe that became mode-based on win32 reddens it.

groups.rootCause: the arm supplies a POSIX shell stub (`fake-detector.sh`) that the row spawns DIRECTLY (`spawnSync(binary, ["check"])`, no shell); win32 has no shebang mechanism, so it fails with `Executable not found in $PATH`. Neither alternative works: node >= 18.20 REFUSES to spawn a `.cmd`/`.bat` without `shell: true`, and the bundle ships no native stub.
groups.fix: a DECLARED INSTRUMENT BOUND: `test.skipIf(process.platform === "win32")` with the reason written out. The arm's SUBJECT (a relative file_path resolved against the SESSION workspace) is platform-independent code, but its instrument is not; the subject stays covered on POSIX.

groups.rootCause: `expect(missing.root).toContain(".mpd/workmate")` — a POSIX literal against a `join`-built root.
the SAME `path.slice(path.lastIndexOf("/") + 1)` basename bug as the unit-test fixtures, so its c7 stage read a present record as `{leading:false, members:0}`.

the 'sibling install' fixture was built with `launched.replace("/profiles/dsh-tui", "/profiles/other")`; on win32 `join` emits `\`, the replace matched NOTHING, so the 'sibling' WAS the launched copy and the arm failed on a CORRECT verdict.
groups.fix: the sibling is built with the separator the launched path itself uses.
